EXCLUSIVE: While Massachuse...
body_text:
Gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue explains how he would expand access, lower costs, tackle the mental health crisis and root out waste in the state's healthcare system.

EXCLUSIVE: While Massachusetts boasts some of the premier hospitals in the world, it also suffers from some of the highest healthcare costs in America.

GOP gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue believes that is no coincidence.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, the former longtime medical devices CEO says the commonwealth can boost access, cut costs and reduce regulation through innovation, as opposed to government mandates.

MIKE MINOGUE HEADS TO MASS GOP CONVENTION READY TO TAKE ON MAURA HEALEY: 'SHE'S BANKRUPTING OUR STATE'

Combat veteran turned CEO Mike Minogue on Wednesday launched a Republican campaign for governor in Massachusetts. (Mike Minogue campaign)

"I think the most important thing that can help health care is to have a 'patients first mindset.' When I was the CEO of Abiomed, everyone rallied around the patients first culture, commitment and every action, every decision that we took really was focused on, ‘does this improve the patient outcome? Does this help the physicians and the nurses make it easier to use? Does it help us save money for the system?’"

He cites the incredibly weighty regulatory burden imposed on nurses and doctors as part of the problem.

"We [must] have a focus that we're really going through areas that allow for patients to get access to their physicians, their nurses, and also utilize innovation, things that are breakthrough, and things that can minimize the burden on the physicians and the nurses with regulations and documentation.

"I'm optimistic because I've seen it firsthand. I've worked with health care systems all over the world. I specifically know how hard physicians and nurses work and they're the heart of that system. So what we're going to focus on is a patients first health care plan that brings access to quality, affordable care."

Healthcare is a top concern for Bay State voters, and Minogue hopes to use the issue to his advantage in a tough battle to challenge incumbent Democrat Governor Maura Healey.He notes that the often stark disparity between healthcare access and quality between the metro Boston area and the rest of the state is a perpetual problem, that needs a remedy:

"Right now, if you look at what's happening around Massachusetts, we're losing innovation and treatment in areas that do not now have opportunity for high-risk procedures, whether it's maternity, cardiac or stroke.

"We have areas now in communities that might have a 50-plus minute drive to get to the nearest area. An example is Norwood. The hospital closed. So if you have a cardiac event in Norwood, you're looking at a 55-minute-plus drive at best to get to Boston."

FILE - Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey also hosted a news conference on Thursday, pushing back on the Supreme Court's decision. (David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

Minogue promises that under his tenure, he will work to improve coverage and care statewide:

"This is the role of the governor—to provide hub-and-spoke innovation in healthcare for the whole Commonwealth, not just Boston."

COMBAT VETERAN TURNED CEO HAS A NEW MISSION: FLIP GOVERNOR'S OFFICE IN BLUE STATE

Yet, Minogue argues, the current system poses not merely a geographic problem, but a fiscal one as well:

"Our regulations strangle the rest of the Commonwealth and almost mandate that all procedures are being done in Boston in the highest-cost environment. If you go to outpatient centers and surgery centers, you reduce the cost of procedures, you lower the overhead, and it's a much easier process than driving all the way into Boston. We have incredible hospitals here, but we also have some of the lowest numbers of outpatient clinics and surgery centers as a state. We need to improve that."Given his business background, Minogue is intimately familiar with the economics of providing healthcare coverage for thousands of families.

"As a CEO, I bought health insurance for 19 years for my employees. I never saw an increase that wasn't double-digit every year…We need to lower the costs.

"We also have to minimize mandating every single treatment and procedure onto every healthcare plan. We need to allow people to have the ability to select what care they want."

FOX NEWS POLL: GOP DIVISIONS SHAPE TEXAS SENATE RACE

Minogue believes patients should have more flexibility in choosing their coverage while ensuring families are protected from financially devastating medical emergencies:

"We do need to cap the catastrophic… At Abiomed, what we did every year is we paid the extra amount so that we would always cap what it would cost the patient. We combined that with a Health Savings Account, which is a great way for people to take more control over their own healthcare plan. Everything that you do in a patients first mindset solves a lot of problems."As a mental health crisis is surging across the state, Minogue has a solution for matching patients and therapists.

"We do have an extensive amount of counselors, but most of them are on private pay…We don't allow general practitioners or counselors to get paid outside of private pay, so that's why most of these patients are going to the emergency rooms.

"It would be simple and more efficient if we also allowed the subsidized government pay to allow those patients to see the same people in the clinics that private-pay people have access to."

Republican Mike Minogue, seen with his wife Renee and their five children, is running for the Republican gubernatorial nomination in Massachusetts  (Mike Minogue campaign)

Minogue's plan has specific provisions for addressing an area where the mental health crisis has been particularly acute:

"One of the areas that I'm most focused on for mental health or PTSD is our correctional facility officers in Massachusetts have some of the highest suicide rates in America.

"We know veterans with PTSD also have high suicide rates. These people are all ending up in emergency rooms, and that's not a very good solution."

Hands-on experience with frontline healthcare workers is what Minogue believes gives his plan the credibility to set the Bay State on the right track again.

"I've been very fortunate because I have a network of physicians and nurses and counselors that have been working with me for months.

"We've collaborated so that we can come up with this patients first plan.

"If you put the patient at the center of that, the treatment plans can be very specialized for better outcomes at lower cost."Finally, Minogue has a specific plan to root out waste and fraud, a particularly timely topic following investigations across the nation that have unveiled a costly web of corruption in social services at the taxpayer's expense:

"The most important thing is to recognize that better outcomes and a patients first mindset actually can reduce costs…But we have an additional area of cost savings. It's called inefficiency, waste and fraud.

"We'll identify inefficiency, excess and fraud, and I believe we're going to find hundreds of millions of dollars in savings at a minimum.

"I'd like to use some of that money as an incentive on outcomes and make sure physicians and nurses can share in the success of improving outcomes. Great quality will lower our costs."

Minogue won the Massachusetts GOP endorsement at the party's state convention in Worcester, and is widely expected to win the Republican Primary on September 1, to face off against incumbent Governor Maura Healey.

David Unsworth reports on Latin America. You can follow David Unsworth on Twitter @LatinAmerUpdate

title: Anthropic says AI models hacked three firms during tests
excerpt: US tech company Anthropic says three of its artificial intelligence (AI) models broke out of isolated test environments and hacked into the systems of three other firms during a cybersecurity exercise...
body_text:
US tech company Anthropic says three of its artificial intelligence (AI) models broke out of isolated test environments and hacked into the systems of three other firms during a cybersecurity exercise.

It comes just days after rival OpenAI said that its models had breached the systems of other companies, including Hugging Face - a hub for AI tools.

The announcement prompted Anthropic to check whether its own models had carried out similar attacks. It says it uncovered three cases that have since been reported to the affected companies.

Anthropic, which did not name the firms, urged other AI labs to perform similar reviews to better understand the risks of their models' capabilities.

Anthropic said in a statement, external that it reviewed more than 140,000 tests to find evidence that Claude - its family of AI models - could access the internet from testing environments that were designed to be sealed off.

The tests include so-called "capture-the-flag" evaluations in which Claude was tasked with obtaining information by breaching other systems - a common way that experts assess a model's hacking capabilities.

A "miscommunication" on systems run by Anthropic and its testing partner left the models with live internet access, allowing them to breach other systems, the San Francisco-based firm said.

Anthropic added that it is "approaching the fixes as if the responsibility were ours alone."

A string of AI-driven cyberattacks has fuelled calls for tighter safeguards and oversight of the technology, over concerns about the risks posed by increasingly powerful autonomous systems.

US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that Washington is considering measures to rein in artificial intelligence tools after recent cybersecurity incidents.

title: Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain
excerpt:
US president’s Board of Peace says Israel will withdraw from Gaza following disarmament of Hamas but no immediate statement from either side

What is Trump’s Board of Peace and who is involved?

Donal...
body_text:
US president’s Board of Peace says Israel will withdraw from Gaza following disarmament of Hamas but no immediate statement from either side

What is Trump’s Board of Peace and who is involved?

Donald Trump on Thursday announced an agreement for the “complete disarmament” of Hamas, calling it a critical step toward a new Palestinian government in Gaza. There was no immediate statement from Hamas or Israel on the agreement.

“This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people,” Trump said in a social media post.

“At the same time, Israel will have ⁠the security it deserves, with Gaza no longer used as a base for terror attacks.”

The Israeli embassy in Washington and Hamas did not immediately respond to requests for comment about Trump’s post.

Sources close to the talks told Reuters earlier on ⁠Thursday that progress was made but it is ⁠uncertain if the agreement will hold, as an ​Israeli official had said the proposed terms were not satisfactory.

“Israel demands the complete disarmament of Hamas, including ​the removal of weapons from Gaza and the complete demilitarisation of the strip as a precondition for ‌any process,” the official said, adding that the plan under discussion did not “provide a satisfactory response to these demands and Israel conveyed its objections.”

Hamas leaders are reportedly holding talks with mediators from Egypt, Qatar and Turkey on the second phase of Trump’s Gaza plan, as ‌presented to them by his Board of Peace, which oversees its implementation.

On Thursday, ‌a Hamas official said the group was coming with a “positive and good” response, but did not say whether the group had agreed to fully disarm – a key sticking point in the talks over the past four months.

Hamas wants Israel to commit to ending attacks on Gaza and withdrawing its forces.

A diplomat involved in the talks said the roadmap under discussion in Cairo would also see authority transferred in phases to the US-backed National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), under the principle of “one authority, one law, one weapon”.

The plan includes the elimination of tunnels, arms stockpiles and weapons production facilities, the diplomat said, adding that by the end of the process there would be no remaining militant infrastructure in Gaza.

The diplomat described the roadmap as being ⁠based on reciprocal steps rather than trust.

So far, the reality on the ground in Gaza remains far from this roadmap.

Israeli strikes killed at least six Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday, including two children, local medics said.

The Israeli military has continued to expand ​its military occupation of Gaza, with the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, saying that Israel intends to ​expand the area under its control to 70% of the territory.

It remains unclear ​how many forces would be available to deploy with the planned International Stabilisation Force, and whether Israeli troops would withdraw from the territory.

title: Anthropic’s AI Claude escaped testing environment and hacked organizations
excerpt:
Company says it discovered unauthorized access during ‘proactive review’ after rival OpenAI revealed rogue agent

Anthropic ⁠said on Thursday its AI Claude model hacked ⁠systems of ⁠three ​organizatio...
body_text:
Company says it discovered unauthorized access during ‘proactive review’ after rival OpenAI revealed rogue agent

Anthropic ⁠said on Thursday its AI Claude model hacked ⁠systems of ⁠three ​organizations during testing, days after rival OpenAI ⁠revealed a rogue agent had gone on a days-long ⁠hacking spree at AI ​firm Hugging ‌Face.

Claude gained ‌unauthorized access to the ‌systems during cybersecurity evaluations after a misconfiguration allowed the models to reach the internet from testing environments that ‌were supposed to be isolated, Anthropic said.

The company said ​it identified the incidents after reviewing 141,006 cybersecurity evaluation runs, a process it ⁠launched following OpenAI’s disclosures.

The ‌breaches signal that AI’s expanding capabilities are already fueling the security threat experts have long feared ‌and that even top developers can be caught off-guard by flaws their models can exploit.

“Claude compromised the ​impacted ​organizations’ infrastructure using ​basic techniques, such as ​exploiting ‌weak passwords and ​unauthenticated ​endpoints,” it said.

Anthropic said the incidents involved three separate models: Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Mythos 5 and an internal research model. The earliest cases dated back to April and ‌occurred in evaluation environments that lacked what the company described as standard safeguards.

The breaches occurred during the so-called “capture the flag” exercises, in which models were tasked with finding ​hidden information in simulated networks. The company said its prompts told the models they had no internet access, but a misunderstanding with its evaluation partner Irregular left the systems connected to the public internet.

Two of the organizations were ​unaware of the activity ‌before being contacted, Anthropic ​said, adding that ​it was still trying to reach the third.

“We discovered these incidents after a proactive review of our cybersecurity evaluation transcripts,” the company said in a statement.

The findings underscore the need for stronger controls in both internal and third-party testing environments as AI models become increasingly capable of carrying out real-world cyber activities, Anthropic said.

title: Sen Mark Kelly warns far-left policies that ‘don’t make sense’ could cost Democrats seats
excerpt:
Sen. Mark Kelly rejected calls to abolish police, eliminate the border and defund the Pentagon, warning that voters’ association with those policies with Democrats could cost the party seats.

Sen. Ma...
body_text:
Sen. Mark Kelly rejected calls to abolish police, eliminate the border and defund the Pentagon, warning that voters’ association with those policies with Democrats could cost the party seats.

Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., said Thursday during an interview on "Next Question with Katie Couric" that far-left calls to abolish police, eliminate prisons and the border and defund the Pentagon were partly responsible for Democrats' low approval ratings because voters associated those positions with the broader party.

"There are folks out there that say things that just don’t make sense to the American people, like abolish the police or get rid of jails and prisons, get rid of the border, defund the Pentagon," Kelly said.

Couric asked Kelly whether the Democratic Party’s ideological divide could hurt its candidates during the midterm elections and its eventual 2028 presidential nominee.

DEM REP HENRY CUELLAR REJECTS DSA AGENDA, SAYS SOCIALISTS ARE TRYING TO 'USE' DEMOCRATIC PARTY

Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., rejected far-left proposals to abolish police, eliminate the border and defund the Pentagon as policies that "don’t make sense." (Jose Luis Magana/ AP)

"It could cost us some seats," Kelly said. "I think that’s very, very possible."

Kelly distanced himself from the party’s left flank, saying voters sometimes attributed its most progressive proposals to every Democratic candidate.

"Some of them, I think, associate it with Democrats," Kelly said. "That’s not the Democratic Party I’m in. Those aren’t the policies I support."

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS WANT MAJOR CHANGE AMID ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL DISCONTENT

Kelly warned that voters’ association with fringe positions by the Democratic Party could cost its candidates seats in the midterm elections. (Heather Diehl/Getty Images)

Kelly's remarks followed months of bleak polling for Democratic leaders. A Fox News poll conducted in April found that 42% of registered voters viewed the Democratic Party favorably, while 58% viewed it unfavorably. Sixty-one percent said Democrats were focused on the "wrong" issues.

A Quinnipiac University poll released in May found that 20% of registered voters approved of the job Democrats in Congress were doing, while 72% disapproved. Even among Democratic voters, 41% approved and 50% disapproved.

Kelly issued his warning after democratic socialist candidates scored several prominent primary victories.

DSA-backed candidate Melat Kiros defeated longtime Rep. Diana DeGette, D-Colo., while DSA member Darializa Avila Chevalier ousted veteran Rep. Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y.

DSA-endorsed New York state lawmaker Claire Valdez also won the Democratic primary to succeed retiring Rep. Nydia Velázquez, D-N.Y.

BERNIE SANDERS, DSA REVEAL DEMANDS FOR DEM PARTY AFTER SOCIALISTS SWEEP NEW YORK ELECTIONS

The Arizona Democrat distanced himself from his party’s left flank as DSA-backed candidates scored several prominent primary victories. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Kelly said he is "seriously considering" a 2028 presidential campaign and that his wife, former Rep. Gabby Giffords, was encouraging him to enter the race. He said his decision would depend on his family and whether he believed he could win.

"She’s about, you know, what’s the best thing for the country?" Kelly said of Giffords. "She is all about public service, and everybody needs to do their part.

"If we come to the conclusion that, you know, I’m the right person for this and my family’s on board, and we also consider what it takes."

The Arizona Democrat has also built a political operation capable of supporting a national campaign, saying he had directed millions of dollars to candidates he considered electable while avoiding campaigns centered on unrealistic proposals.

"I have the ability to, you know, raise money. I'm pretty good at that," Kelly said.

"I have raised or given away combined $10 million during this election cycle," he continued. "I tend to steer away from the stuff that is never going to happen, that is just about creating a lot of noise."

Despite the party’s poor image, a Fox News poll released last week found Democrats leading Republicans by seven points among registered voters, 53% to 46%.

The poll also found that 68% of Democrats were extremely motivated to vote in November, compared with 57% of Republicans. Democratic support was the highest either party had recorded on Fox News’ generic congressional ballot since 1996.

title: WATCH: GOP holdout rejects Trump threat as AG nominee standoff explodes
excerpt: Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., responds to President Trump's threat to pull Todd Blanche's nomination, saying negotiations continue and blaming the White House for the stalled confirmation process. (Credit...
body_text:
Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., responds to President Trump's threat to pull Todd Blanche's nomination, saying negotiations continue and blaming the White House for the stalled confirmation process. (Credit: Nicholas Ballasy for Fox News Digital)

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., brushed aside President Donald Trump's threat to withdraw acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's nomination on Thursday, arguing the White House must instead honor what he says was an earlier commitment to win his vote.

"That's his prerogative," Tillis said about Trump’s threat to withdraw Blanche’s nomination.

Tillis’ comments come after Trump called out both Tillis and Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, on Truth Social Thursday morning for blocking the president’s efforts to make Blanche the nation’s top prosecutor. He then threatened to pull Blanche’s nomination until the two Republican senators leave office next year — as Tillis is retiring and Cornyn lost his primary in his run for re-election.

TRUMP THREATENS TO YANK HIS OWN AG NOMINEE AS GOP REVOLT GROWS

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., is brushing off President Donald Trump's threat to pull Todd Blanche's nomination, insisting negotiations remain ongoing. (Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images; Ken Cedeno/AFP via Getty Images)

Tillis argued Trump cannot resolve this nomination standoff "unless we fulfill what we thought was the commitment from the administration."

The North Carolina senator has withheld his support for Blanche unless the administration agrees to permanently eliminate the nearly $2 billion anti-weaponization fund and rewrite Trump's audit immunity language in the settlement agreement. Negotiations over those demands remain ongoing.

"The best thing is, take the win, get Blanche confirmed and get this agreement out of the way," Tillis told Fox News Digital.

When asked what it would take to get Tillis to vote to confirm Blanche, he said, "exactly what Blanche committed to."

TRUMP ADMIN PUSHES BACK ON 'SLUSH FUND' ATTACKS AGAINST ANTI-WEAPONIZATION FUND AND LAYS OUT WHO QUALIFIES

Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche appears at a confirmation hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., July 15, 2026. (Eric Lee/Getty Images)

Tillis stressed that Blanche himself is not to blame for the impasse, saying he believes he "was honest" during his confirmation process and that he blames someone on Trump’s team.

"This is not Blanche's problem. It's clear to me that Blanche was honest when he answered without hesitation, working with us to end this," Tillis said.

He continued, "I believe that one of the president's advisors who were part of this agreement is the problem. And they need to own it."

Tillis also pointed out that there is no certainty that the Senate would be any more accepting of Blanche next year, particularly as Republicans have more seats in danger than Democrats in the Senate.

"The best case scenario is you come back with the same number of people next year, and our members are not going to be any more supportive of this than they are today."

TRUMP-TILLIS TIFF DEEPENS AS PRESIDENT SAYS HE ‘QUIT,’ CONCEDES FED FIGHT COULD DOOM NEW CHAIR CONFIRMATION

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., makes his way to a vote in the U.S. Capitol on Thursday, April 30, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc)

Trump could still keep Blanche as acting attorney general for months even if he withdraws the nomination. The Federal Vacancies Reform Act allows acting officials to serve for 210 days, and withdrawing a pending nomination resets that clock. If Trump were to pull Blanche's nomination Thursday, Blanche could remain in the role until late February.

Despite Trump's public threat, Tillis said negotiations with the administration remain ongoing and said he is "not a no" on Blanche.

"In this place, nothing's ever as good or as bad as it seems, so we're continuing to negotiate," Tillis said.

Fox News Digital’s Alex Miller and Adam Pack contributed to this report.

Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.

title: Influencer accused of targeting wealthy dating app matches back behind bars
excerpt: Elaine Angene Escoe, on the run since May 2025, was captured in Jamaica while living under a fake identity of 'Harley Newman' and returned to the United States today to face justice. FBI Director Kash...
body_text:
Elaine Angene Escoe, on the run since May 2025, was captured in Jamaica while living under a fake identity of 'Harley Newman' and returned to the United States today to face justice. FBI Director Kash Patel emphasized the historic success of the 'Most Wanted Fraudster' list, noting Escoe is the fourth such capture in five weeks.

A Los Angeles influencer accused of targeting wealthy victims before stealing from them is back behind bars after authorities said she allegedly removed her ankle monitor while awaiting trial.

Adva Lavie, 28, who also goes by Mia Ventura, was arrested Tuesday night in Beverly Hills just months after she was released on electronic monitoring while awaiting trial on felony burglary charges.

Prosecutors said Lavie violated the conditions of her release by allegedly removing the electronic monitor she was ordered to wear. A judge has since revoked her release, ordered her held without bail and scheduled a bail review hearing for Friday in Van Nuys.

Court records also show Lavie was arrested on an outstanding Riverside County warrant in a separate grand theft case.

NEARLY 1 IN 12 DEFENDANTS ON ANKLE MONITORS IN CHICAGO HAVE GONE AWOL, AUTHORITIES SAY

Adva Lavie, also known as Mia Ventura, is shown in a Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department special bulletin. (Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department)

Newly obtained court records show Riverside County prosecutors charged Lavie in April with felony grand theft after accusing her of stealing more than $11,000 in luxury items during the 2025 Coachella Music Festival.

Prosecutors said Lavie failed to appear for her scheduled May arraignment, prompting a judge to issue a $20,000 arrest warrant. As of Thursday afternoon, she had not yet been booked into Riverside County, and no in-custody arraignment had been scheduled.

HOMEOWNERS IN LEAFY ENCLAVES HIT BY BURGLARS ZEROING IN ON HIGH-END HOMES FOR SMASH-AND-GRAB SCORES

Adva Lavie, also known as Mia Ventura, is shown in a Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department special bulletin alongside vehicles authorities said were linked to a residential burglary series targeting victims through dating apps. (Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department)

The Riverside case centers on allegations Lavie stole an approximately $8,600 Rolex watch, Louis Vuitton Aviator sunglasses valued at about $700 and a Louis Vuitton cardholder worth about $1,800 from a man she attended Coachella with.

Investigators said the man invited Lavie to stay with him at an Airbnb in Indio during Coachella weekend. After the pair argued, she allegedly helped herself to the luxury items from his unlocked Tesla Cybertruck before leaving.

According to an arrest warrant, surveillance cameras at the Airbnb captured the alleged theft, and detectives later identified Lavie from the video. Investigators also noted she was a suspect in another theft reported at the same property.

FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES

Adva Lavie, also known as Mia Ventura, in modeling photos. (Paul Archuleta/Getty Images for Teatro Live; Paul Archuleta/Getty Images)

Lavie's latest arrest comes nearly four months after Los Angeles County prosecutors accused her of carrying out a dating app burglary spree targeting wealthy victims across Southern California.

Prosecutors allege Lavie spent years using dating apps and "Sugar Daddy" websites to build relationships with wealthy older men and younger women before posing as a girlfriend or travel companion to gain access to their homes.

Adva Lavie, also known as Mia Ventura, in red carpet and event photos. (Paul Archuleta/Getty Images; Paul Archuleta/Getty Images for Teatro Live; Paul Archuleta/Getty Images for Teatro)

Once inside, authorities said, she stole cash, gold, credit cards and luxury designer items from victims in Westlake Village, West Hollywood, Los Angeles and Beverly Hills.

Lavie has pleaded not guilty to six felony charges, including two counts of grand theft, two counts of first-degree residential burglary and two counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information. She was released from custody on an electronic ankle monitor before her latest arrest.

When announcing the case in March, Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said prosecutors intended to prove Lavie exploited the trust she built through online relationships.

Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman speaks at a news conference alongside Los Angeles County Sheriff Robert Luna June 11, 2025, in Los Angeles. (KTTV)

"At her trial, we will prove beyond a reasonable doubt that this defendant exploited trust built through online relationships to gain access to victims' homes and steal from them," Hochman said. "Her ability to deceptively influence others, whether in person or online, has now come to an end."

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department previously released a public bulletin identifying Lavie as the suspect in the dating app burglary investigation and published photographs of luxury vehicles investigators said she drove, including a white Mercedes-Benz coupe and a black Porsche SUV.

Fox 11 Los Angeles previously reported that Lavie's fiancé, billionaire entrepreneur Stephen Cloobeck, was arrested on separate felony charges alleging he attempted to dissuade witnesses from testifying against her.

If convicted on all six felony counts in the Los Angeles County case, Lavie faces up to 11 years and eight months in state prison.

Fox News Digital's Michael Dorgan contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: WNBA fans call out glaring double standard after Angel Reese’s clueless response to Paige Bueckers bet
excerpt:
The WNBA media will not treat Paige Bueckers and Caitlin Clark the same even though they keep saying they will.

Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese doesn't care about the PR damage control the WNBA is cur...
body_text:
The WNBA media will not treat Paige Bueckers and Caitlin Clark the same even though they keep saying they will.

Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese doesn't care about the PR damage control the WNBA is currently going through.

The WNBA was mercilessly criticized Wednesday after sharing, then deleting, a video featuring Reese and Wings player Paige Bueckers.

The league's social media team inadvertently highlighted one of the most sensitive issues in professional sports: gambling.

WNBA ADMITS CONTROVERSIAL BETTING VIDEO FEATURING ANGEL REESE, PAIGE BUECKERS 'MISSED THE MARK'

Reese and Bueckers agreed to a $400 bet ahead of Wednesday's matchup in Arlington.

After the Dream's narrow 82-81 win, Reese shrugged off the controversy when asked about the wager.

"Yeah, I’ll be requesting my Apple Pay after this," Reese said postgame.

Team Collier stands for the national anthem before the game against Team Clark during the AT&T WNBA All-Star Game 2025 on July 19, 2025 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Ind. (NBAE via Getty Images)

Critics questioned whether this kind of "lighthearted" banter would ever fly in leagues like the NBA.

Others wondered whether Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham would've received the same treatment. Just look at the firestorm surrounding Cunningham, then ask whether the sports media is holding Reese and Cunningham to the same standard.

EX-FORDHAM BASKETBALL PLAYERS PERMANENTLY BANNED BY NCAA OVER ALLEGED GAME MANIPULATION BETTING SCHEME

"[Reese] only admitted it because it was filmed, who knows what other games she bet on?" one critic wrote.

Another chimed in: "I wonder what the WNBA would have done if it was Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham making a $400 wager on a game they are playing in instead of Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers?"

Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream guards Paige Bueckers of the Dallas Wings as Bueckers drives in the second half of a WNBA game at College Park Center on July 29, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. (Getty Images)

Under Section 5(c) of the WNBA's Collective Bargaining Agreement, players are strictly prohibited from placing wagers, directly, indirectly, or even as a side bet, on any league game. Violations give the commissioner broad authority to impose severe penalties, ranging from fines and suspensions to permanent banishment in order to protect the integrity of the league.

The post sparked immediate questions about potential violations of the league's anti-gambling policy, prompting the WNBA to release a statement addressing the deleted clip on Thursday (as reported by OutKick's Mark Harris).

The league characterized it as a "lighthearted exchange" and announced no discipline.

"While the social media post was intended to be lighthearted, WNBA players are well aware of the league's policies prohibiting betting on WNBA games and receive training every year reinforcing those policies," the statement read.

OutKick reached out for comment on its internal decision-making. We have not received a response.

Paige Bueckers of the Dallas Wings has a brief exchange with Angel Reese of the Atlanta Dream during a WNBA game at College Park Center on July 29, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. (Getty Images)

"We recognized that the post missed the mark, removed it shortly after it was published, and addressed the matter internally. We will also use this as an opportunity to reemphasize with the players involved that conversations about wagering on WNBA games, even when intended as a joke, can have negative consequences."

Deleting the video solved an immediate public relations problem, but it also compromised the league's standard.

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

title: Hamas says it has agreed to disarm after Trump announces Board of Peace plan
excerpt:
US President Donald Trump says the Board of Peace has reached an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.

A senior Hamas official has told the BBC they have a...
body_text:
US President Donald Trump says the Board of Peace has reached an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.

A senior Hamas official has told the BBC they have agreed to the Board of Peace's plan to completely disarm in Gaza and that an official statement will be released soon. Israel has yet to comment.

Trump said Israel would withdraw from Gaza "as disarmament is completed" and called the agreement "a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government".

The second phase of a US-brokered Gaza ceasefire plan includes the disarmament of Hamas.

The second phase also includes the reconstruction of Gaza.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said: "This is a major milestone in the implementation of the Trump 20-Point Plan. The agreement will be carried out in carefully structured phases. As disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will withdraw, and the International Stabilization Force will work with a new Palestinian police force to take responsibility for Gaza being safe for its residents and its neighbors."

He also thanked mediators Egypt, Qatar and Turkey.

Cairo would host a Gaza mediator meeting on the second phase of the ceasefire plan, Agence France-Presse reported, citing Egyptian state media.

Earlier in the day, unnamed sources who spoke to Reuters reported that talks between the mediators and Hamas leaders in Cairo on implementing the US-brokered Gaza peace plan had made rare progress, but an Israeli official said the proposed terms were not satisfactory.

Following Trump's announcement, the Times of Israel reported, citing an unnamed source, that the agreement had been signed between negotiators from Hamas as well as the board and mediating countries.

But it said that "an Israeli office" issued a statement saying the disarmament proposal did not meet Jerusalem's demands.

Earlier in the day, Israeli media reported that Israel was opposed to a deal that was being discussed with Hamas.

In April this year, Hamas rejected the disarmament plan of a top figure in Trump's Gaza peace efforts, a senior Palestinian official familiar with the negotiations told the BBC.

Earlier this month, Hamas elected a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya. He replaced Yahya Sinwar, who was killed by the Israeli military in Gaza in October 2024. As the chief negotiator for Hamas, Hayya led the group's delegations at indirect ceasefire talks, meeting mediators in Egypt and Qatar.

The BBC reported earlier this year that the board was originally thought to be aimed at helping end the war between Israel and Hamas in Gaza and oversee reconstruction. But its proposed charter does not mention the Palestinian territory and appears to be designed to supplant functions of the UN.

Hamas led an attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, in which 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.

Israel responded by launching a massive military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 73,290 people have been killed, including 21,280 children, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

title: Mandela Barnes drops out of high-stakes Wisconsin governor’s race
excerpt:
Former lieutenant governor says path to Democratic nomination no longer viable as democratic socialist rival surges ahead

Mandela Barnes, the former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, dropped out of t...
body_text:
Former lieutenant governor says path to Democratic nomination no longer viable as democratic socialist rival surges ahead

Mandela Barnes, the former lieutenant governor of Wisconsin, dropped out of the Democratic primary for governor on Thursday, upending the high-stakes contest less than two weeks before the 11 August election.

Barnes announced the decision in a video posted on social media, saying he no longer saw a viable path to the nomination as democratic socialist Francesca Hong surged ahead with a commanding lead.

“It’s become very clear who our nominee is going to be,” Barnes, 39, said.

The Marquette Law School poll showed Hong significantly ahead of Barnes in a distant second place, with 38% compared to his 16%, having consolidated liberal support, especially among young voters, although about a third of primary voters remained undecided.

Soon after Barnes’s withdrawal, the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported it had sent questions to the candidate about past allegations of inappropriate behavior that had been anonymously submitted to the Wisconsin Democratic party, local party officials and others.

According to the Journal Sentinel, the state party hired a law firm in 2025 to investigate the claims sent in a letter that Barnes had used his position in the party to pursue inappropriate relationships with “young adult women”.

The party’s internal review and outside investigation found no actionable evidence because the claims were “anonymous and unspecific”, the Journal Sentinel reported, citing an unnamed person familiar with the matter.

“There are no allegations of misconduct or wrongdoing against Mandela,” it said in a statement.

His departure adds another twist in the Democratic primary for governor in Wisconsin, a perennial presidential battleground that has also been at the center of national disputes over election administration since the 2020 election.

He is the third Democrat to exit the race, following lieutenant governor Sara Rodriguez, who withdrew two weeks ago amid a campaign finance scandal. After Rodriguez’s exit, Milwaukee county executive David Crowley re-entered the race with the endorsement of Governor Tony Evers, who is not seeking re-election.

Earlier this summer, Missy Hughes, a former state economic development director, ended her campaign.

On Wednesday, a judge rejected an effort backed by the Democratic party to let voters who had already cast absentee ballots void their initial vote and vote again, over concerns that many early ballots had been cast for candidates who were no longer in the race.

Crowley moved quickly to appeal to Barnes’s supporters: “There’s a place for you in what we’re building.”

Evers told reporters he was surprised by Barnes’s decision to withdraw but reiterated his support for Crowley, saying he believed Crowley was the strongest candidate “even if Mandela was in”, the Associated Press reported.

The Democratic gubernatorial nominee in Wisconsin is expected to face Republican US congressman Tom Tiffany, who is backed by Donald Trump.

Barnes was once viewed as a rising star in Democratic politics. In 2022, rather than seek re-election as lieutenant governor, he ran for the US Senate, narrowly losing the race to incumbent Republican Ron Johnson.

title: Hiker's unexplained death exposes deadly alcohol withdrawal risk many don't recognize
excerpt:
The actor explained that his wife gave him an ultimatum when it came to his drinking, which ultimately got him to stop.

When hiker Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, was found dead near Sykes Hot Springs in Ca...
body_text:
The actor explained that his wife gave him an ultimatum when it came to his drinking, which ultimately got him to stop.

When hiker Joanna Ruth Shields, 37, was found dead near Sykes Hot Springs in California’s Ventana Wilderness, initial speculation pointed to foul play, according to a press release from the Monterey County Sheriff's Office.

However, official coroner's reports revealed her cause of death to be probable alcohol withdrawal seizures brought on by chronic alcohol use disorder.

Friends who were hiking with Shields said she had gone to the river that morning. A short time later, one of them found her unresponsive in the water, according to reports.

IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

"This is a probable seizure that occurred as a result of chronic alcohol use disorder, but there was nothing that stood out that indicated any type of criminal activity," Andres Rosas, commander and the primary public information officer for the Monterey County Sheriff's Office, told KSBW 8.

Given the results of the investigation and forensic examination, no further investigation is taking place.

The recent death of a Big Sur hiker was ruled a probable case of fatal alcohol withdrawal seizures, exposing a dangerous and often hidden medical crisis. (iStock)

The incident highlights a little-known danger of severe alcohol dependence, as suddenly stopping alcohol can trigger life-threatening neurological events.

Alcohol acts as a depressant on the central nervous system. When someone drinks heavily over a prolonged period, the brain adapts by ramping up chemical signals to keep bodily systems functioning, according to experts.

When alcohol is abruptly stopped, that blocker on the central nervous system is removed. The brain then enters a state of dangerous overexcitation, leading to severe hyperarousal.

Withdrawal symptoms typically begin within six to 24 hours after the last drink, with the risk of seizures peaking between 24 and 48 hours.

Alcohol withdrawal can quickly progress from tremors, sweating and anxiety to severe grand mal seizures and a condition called Delirium Tremens. (iStock)

In wilderness settings or isolated locations, a sudden seizure can result in immediate loss of consciousness, trauma, respiratory arrest or an inability to seek emergency care, experts note.

Clinical guidelines from the National Institutes of Health categorize alcohol withdrawal by the following key progression stages.

This may include minor withdrawal symptoms, including insomnia, tremors, anxiety, gastrointestinal upset, headache, diaphoresis (excessive sweating), heart palpitations, anorexia, nausea, tachycardia (abnormally fast resting heart rate) and hypertension.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

This stage is marked by visual, auditory or tactile hallucinations.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

People in this stage may experience sudden loss of consciousness accompanied by severe muscle contractions (seizures). Another potential symptom is delirium tremens, a medical emergency involving extreme agitation, fever, racing heart, hyperthermia and cardiac instability.

Attempting to detox without medical supervision can result in sudden loss of consciousness, trauma and death, experts warn. (iStock)

Health agencies, including the National Institutes of Health, strongly advise that individuals with a history of heavy drinking or prior withdrawal episodes should never attempt to detox alone or in remote settings.

Medical detox programs use tailored medication protocols to safely taper brain activity and prevent seizures.

Help is available for people struggling with alcohol use disorder. The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) National Helpline provides free, confidential treatment referrals 24 hours a day at 1-800-662-4357.

Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

title: Saints lock up Chris Olave with 4-year extension worth $132M after training camp hold-in

body_text:
Chris Myers and Mark Schlereth praised the Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints futures in NFC South matchup.

New Orleans Saints star receiver Chris Olave agreed to a four-year extension worth $132 million with $90 million guaranteed, sources confirmed to OutKick’s Armando Salguero.

Olave was set to play the 2026 NFL season on his fifth-year option, and he was a hold-in at training camp because of it. He wanted a new deal before taking part in practices.

The Saints decided to reward their 2022 first-rounder with his desired extension before potential free agency in 2027.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) walks on the sideline during the second half at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Oct. 5, 2025. (Stephen Lew/Imagn Images)

Olave will remain a cornerstone piece for the franchise alongside new starting quarterback Tyler Shough , whom they drafted in the second round in 2025.

This deal marks the highest one the Saints have dished out to a receiver since Michael Thomas received a five-year pact worth up to $20 million per season in 2019. At the time, it was a record.

DRAKE LONDON SIGNS $141M DEAL WITH FALCONS, BECOMING THIRD HIGHEST-PAID RECEIVER IN NFL: REPORTS

Now, Olave will be making $33 million per season, cementing him as one of the highest-paid receivers in the NFL.

The Ohio State product earned that over his rookie deal with the Saints, especially this past season. Across 16 games, Olave notched career-highs in yards (1,163), touchdowns (nine) and receptions (100).

Chris Olave of the New Orleans Saints celebrates after a touchdown during a game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on Dec. 28, 2025, in Nashville, Tenn. The Saints defeated the Titans 34-26. (Getty Images)

Olave started thriving once Shough took over as the team’s starting quarterback, quickly finding chemistry with his new signal caller, and the Saints clearly believe that connection will lead them to playoff glory once more.

The Saints have not reached the playoffs since the 2020 campaign, though they have sprinkled in 9-8 seasons in there. However, they’ve gone 11-23 across the past two seasons, and head coach Kellen Moore’s first year was a 6-11 finish in New Orleans.

But there were positives that came out of the lackluster record, with the offense being the main highlight. The Saints are excited to see what Shough can do with a full offseason understanding he’s the starting quarterback as well as working more in Moore’s system.

Chris Olave of the New Orleans Saints reacts during training camp at Ochsner Sports Performance Center in Metairie, La., on July 30, 2026. (Getty Images)

Olave benefitted from said system, and the Saints bolstered their offensive weapons by signing Travis Etienne Jr. to their backfield. With Saints legend Alvin Kamara returning for another season, the running backs depth chart is filled with explosive playmakers, while Olave, tight end Juwan Johnson, and 2026 first-round pick Jordan Tyson out of Arizona State have this group primed for success.

“This agreement is a critica...
body_text:
United States President Donald Trump has said that his ‘Board of Peace’ has reached an agreement to disarm the Palestinian group Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza.

“This agreement is a critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government that will work closely with the Board of Peace to help the Palestinian people,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social website on Thursday. “At the same time, Israel will have the security it deserves, with Gaza no longer used as a base for terror attacks.”

Hamas has not yet commented on the statement.

Trump framed the disarmament as part of the ceasefire deal he brokered in October to end Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians and devastated the Palestinian enclave. Israel has repeatedly violated the ceasefire agreement, killing more than 1,200 Palestinians, seizing more territory, and continuing to restrict the movement of people and goods into and out of Gaza.

Trump said that Israel would withdraw from Gaza and be replaced by an International Stabilisation Force working with a “new Palestinian police force” once disarmament was complete.

“Under this agreement, Gaza will finally be in the hands of a new Palestinian government that serves its PEOPLE,” Trump added.

Hamas leaders have been in the Egyptian capital Cairo since late last week discussing the ceasefire deal with mediators from Egypt, Qatar, and Turkiye. An unnamed Hamas official was quoted earlier on Thursday as saying that the talks were “positive” and “making progress”.

Hamas had announced on July 6 the dissolution of the body it led that had governed Gaza for nearly two decades.

title: Schiff-backed candidate abruptly ends gubernatorial campaign amid rumblings of a damaging report
excerpt:
Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong was asked about appearing on far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's livestream on MS NOW Wednesday.

Mandela Barnes, who served as Lt. Gover...
body_text:
Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong was asked about appearing on far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's livestream on MS NOW Wednesday.

Mandela Barnes, who served as Lt. Governor of Wisconsin from 2019 to 2023, suspended his gubernatorial campaign on Thursday, citing a lack of support to capture the Democratic Party nomination.

"It’s become very clear who our nominee is going to be," Barnes said in a video statement.

"While I may be suspending my campaign, I’ll never give up my fight for Wisconsin," he continued.

WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO ‘ABOLISH POLICE’

Then-Senate candidate Mandela Barnes is seen leaving a canvas launch event on Nov. 7, 2022, in Glendale, Wisconsin. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

Barnes, who was endorsed by Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., as the "kind of bold leader we need to take on the Trump Administration," did not name the candidate he believes will capture the party’s nomination later this month.

His departure from the race comes as a surprise amid a crowded Democratic field to fill the empty seat of outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers. Barnes was considered a frontrunner in the race because of his proximity to Evers and his name recognition. It also coincides with rumblings that Barnes may have abused his position in the past to make sexual advances towards women in the workplace—an allegation currently under investigation by the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, which published its report shortly after Barnes' video post.

Barnes' campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on if his decision to suspend the campaign was in any way connected to the reporting. However, a Barnes spokesperson told Politico that "there are no allegations of misconduct or wrongdoing against Mandela."

With Barnes’ departure, the remaining major candidates include Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong, a Democratic socialist, and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley.

TOP DEM HOPEFUL FLIPS SCRIPT AFTER YEARS IN SOCIALIST ORBIT WITH PUZZLING CLAIM

Congressman Adam Schiff speaks at the "Just Majority" Burbank Press Conference on May 26, 2023 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Jerod Harris/Getty Images for Demand Justice) (Jerod Harris/Getty Images for Demand Justice)

Notably, Hong has received backing from a number of nationally recognized progressives, including Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif. She has raised nearly $709,000 as of late June, according to state records.

By comparison, Crowley has secured $250,000 and enjoys the support of a number of local organizations and figures.

Evers, pointedly, endorsed Crowley over Barnes, citing Crowley’s experience.

In his departure video, Barnes urged Democrats to unite against Republicans in the November general election.

"Now I said from the very beginning when I launched this campaign that the no. 1 goal was taking on and defeating Tom Tiffany to deliver big wins for Democrats up and down the ticket," Barnes said, referring to the presumptive Republican nominee.

"Now it’s our time to come together and focus our efforts on that one goal. We have to do everything to be Tom Tiffany. This is life or death for Wisconsinites who are losing their healthcare under a Trump administration."

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Wisc., speaks during a television interview outside of the Capitol after being sworn in as a member of Congress on Tuesday, May 19, 2020. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

Barnes built his campaign on a platform of increasing taxes on the country’s top earners, freezing energy costs, providing universal childcare and lowering the cost of housing.

The gubernatorial primary will take place on Aug. 11.

Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

A Florida father and the mother of his children are behind bars after police said they failed to seek emergency care when a 2-year-old girl turned blue, suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally after allegedly ingesting kratom pills.

Jerome Jonathon Jordan, 35, and Charlene Rea O'Connell, 32, are each charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and child neglect causing great bodily harm in the death of 2-year-old Jonnie Jordan, according to the West Melbourne Police Department.

The charges come more than two months after Jonnie was rushed to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne on May 18.

STEPDAD ACCUSED OF SEX ASSAULT AS COPS WIDEN PROBE INTO GIRL’S LETHAL BENADRYL INGREDIENT DOSE

Jerome Jordan and Charlene O'Connell were booked into the Brevard County Jail on charges including aggravated manslaughter of a child. (West Melbourne Police Department)

Investigators said the tragedy unfolded the night before at O'Connell's Palm Bay home, where Jonnie allegedly got into kratom pills belonging to Jordan and O'Connell.

Police said they believe the toddler consumed as many as two-and-a-half pills before both adults realized what had happened.

According to investigators, Jordan and O'Connell watched as Jonnie's lips turned blue, she suffered a seizure and began breathing abnormally. But instead of calling 911 or taking the little girl to a hospital, police allege they failed to seek medical care.

DAYCARE OPERATOR ARRESTED AFTER 3-YEAR-OLD WAS LEFT UNCONSCIOUS IN POOL FOR 20 MINUTES, DIED

The West Melbourne Police Department announced the arrests following its investigation into the toddler's death. (West Melbourne Police Department)

Authorities said Jordan then drove Jonnie back to his sister's apartment in West Melbourne and put her to bed.

Hours later, after waking up and finding the toddler unresponsive, Jordan rushed her to the hospital, where doctors pronounced her dead.

Investigators said Jordan initially urged hospital staff to administer Narcan, leading detectives to suspect an overdose early in the investigation.

SHARON STONE'S TERRIFYING WEED WITHDRAWAL SPARKS WARNING ABOUT TODAY'S POTENT MARIJUANA

An aerial view of Florida's Space Coast near West Melbourne, where police investigated the death of a 2-year-old child. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

The Brevard County  Medical Examiner's Office determined that Jonnie died of acute mitragynine intoxication, according to police.

According to the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, part of the National Institutes of Health, kratom is a herbal substance made from the leaves of a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia and is commonly sold in powders, capsules, gummies and drinks.

Some people use it for its stimulant or pain-relieving effects, though federal health officials have repeatedly warned about its safety.

This Sept. 27, 2017 file photo shows kratom capsules in Albany, N.Y. (AP Photo/Mary Esch, File)

While kratom remains legal under federal law, the Drug Enforcement Administration announced earlier this month it had begun the process of temporarily placing high-potency 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products and certain related synthetic compounds into Schedule I, citing their high potential for abuse and opioid-like effects. The action does not apply to natural kratom leaf products.

Following the medical examiner's findings and a months-long investigation, police arrested Jordan and O'Connell on Thursday. Both are being held without bond at the Brevard County Jail.

Police said Jordan's sister, whose apartment Jonnie was taken to after leaving O'Connell's home, is not facing any charges.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Indiana's Curt Cignetti roasts the SEC as ESPN starts their promotional campaign already: 'we don't whine'
excerpt:
Will Stein discussed his team's schedule and notes that he'd love to only have to play 8 conference games instead of the mandatory 9.

The 2026 college football season hasn't even started, and the war...
body_text:
Will Stein discussed his team's schedule and notes that he'd love to only have to play 8 conference games instead of the mandatory 9.

The 2026 college football season hasn't even started, and the war of words and messaging is already ramping up.

The SEC this year moves to nine conference games, a large shift that will necessarily impact win-loss records and takes away one of their biggest advantages over the Big Ten or other nine-game conferences. As a result, at SEC media days recently, several coaches and even conference commissioner Greg Sankey started their promotional and excuse campaign for the College Football Playoff.

Despite not reaching the National Championship game for three straight seasons and going 2-7 in the playoff against other Power 4 conference teams, the SEC has started their campaign by saying that they deserve more teams in the tournament. Why? Because of their depth and strength of schedule.

SEC WANTS MORE PLAYOFF FAVORITISM AS GREG SANKEY COMPLAINS ABOUT 'UNSATISFACTORY' TALKS WITH CFB PLAYOFF

Sure, depth and strength of schedule matters, but winning your games matters too. And that's where the SEC coaches and Sankey are going through a bit of a contradictory crisis.

SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey speaks to the press during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott in Tampa, Fla., on July 20, 2026. (Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images)

When the SEC was dominant, winning title after title, the narrative went that the depth meant that their teams were battle hardened by playoff time. Other conferences didn't progress through the regular season gauntlet of SEC teams, making them less prepared at the end of the year.

Now that the SEC has fallen behind the Big Ten and are moving to nine conference games, the narrative-building has changed. Just listen to ESPN's Laura Rutledge make excuses for a season and schedule that hasn't happened yet.

LANE KIFFIN MAKES RIDICULOUS EXCUSES FOR SEC'S POOR RECENT PERFORMANCE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

"So, I think one of the reasons why the SEC may not have advanced as far in the playoffs as some SEC fans would like to see," Rutledge told Pat McAfee recently. "It's because the competition within the league is so difficult that nine games of craziness week in and week out are little different than other parts of other conferences. I'm not dissing on the Big 10.

"By the time they get to the end, there are not many left. For one, they eliminate each other, but furthermore, they're gassed. They're injured. They have issues. I'm not making excuses. I'm just pointing out facts because you were pointing out facts," she continued.

"I'm not making excuses," then makes excuses. Because ESPN is heavily invested in promoting the SEC, as their biggest media partners.

ESPN announcer Paul Finebaum before the 2024 SEC Championship game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Dec. 7, 2024. (Brett Davis/Imagn Images)

First, we have yet to see what a nine-game schedule does to the SEC. Second, implying that the previous eight-game schedule was just too much for these teams to handle is actually an argument against the strength of the conference. Third, what happened to the SEC being so battle hardened they could handle the rigors of a playoff run? Now they're just too tired.

Let's look at the 2024 Ohio State National Championship team as a counterpoint, shall we? The Buckeyes in 2024 had road games at Oregon, ranked No. 3 in the country at the time, and Penn State, which was also then ranked No. 3. It hosted No. 5 Indiana and finished with an always tough, physical, rivalry game against a solid Michigan team. It played three playoff teams in the regular season, including the No. 1 overall seed, Oregon, and another physical opponent in Iowa. All within seven weeks. Sounds pretty tough!

They then blew out a vaunted SEC team, Tennessee, 42-17, easily handled another top SEC team, Texas, and beat a very good Notre Dame team in the championship game. That's what good teams do. Indiana in 2025 played Ohio State to finish the season, then blew out Alabama, Oregon, and handled Miami to win a title. That's what good teams do.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Stop making excuses and win important games.

Speaking of excuses and Indiana, if there's one head coach who hates them more than anyone, it's Curt Cignetti. The defending champ took a very pointed shot at the SEC and the excuses culture they've created.

Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti speaks during news conference ahead of the College Football Playoff national championship game between Miami and Indiana, Sunday, Jan. 18, 2026, in Miami. The game will be played on Monday. (AP Photo/Chris Carlson)

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

"I mean we don’t run a hype machine up here in the Midwest," Cignetti said on Thursday at Big Ten media days. "We believe everything’s earned, not given. And when we fall short, we say, ‘We fell short.’ We don’t cry a river, whine and complain. All right? And that’s why we’re the best."

Though, to be fair to the SEC, Notre Dame's in the Midwest and boy oh boy did they cry a river, whine, and complain after getting left out of the playoff last season.

He has a point though, about the current strategy around the SEC. For some reason, instead of saying, "hey, we believe we're the best, we'll go through whatever gauntlet we have in front of us, and beat people up in the playoff, because we're the best," they're saying "woe is us, it's just too tough to win games."

Maybe that's the reason the SEC has fallen behind, because they're consumed with talking about the difficult of playing road games at Mississippi State instead of Nebraska. Or Kentucky instead of Wisconsin. Maybe focus on winning, it's a guarantee the rest will take care of itself.

title: Chris Hemsworth shares terrifying footage from 'crazy' plane ride through lightning and severe turbulence
excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
